common_name: Valentine's Crush Hardy Hibiscus (Cherry-Red Columnar Perennial Hibiscus, Summerific Series)

planting.note: Plant container plants or divisions in spring in consistently moist, fertile soil in full sun.

directions: Bred by Walters Gardens as a brighter-flowered successor to Cranberry Crush in the Summerific series, this cultivar opens cherry-red flowers that lie perfectly flat, on large ovate green leaves that pick up a dark bronze cast in full sun. The sturdy, upright, columnar clump resists lodging, adding up to an inch of new growth a day once it emerges, later than most perennials, in late spring. Grow in full sun with consistently moist, fertile soil and expect vigorous, non-stop bloom from midsummer to frost.

common_name: Lilac Crush Hardy Hibiscus (Rare Lilac-Flowered Columnar Perennial Hibiscus, Summerific Series)

planting.note: Plant container plants or divisions in spring in consistently moist, fertile soil in full sun.

directions: A rare color break for hardy hibiscus, this Walters Gardens Summerific introduction opens thick-textured lilac flowers with overlapping petals that trend cooler in tone during cool weather, set against rich green, maple-like leaves. The upright, columnar habit is sturdy and resists lodging. Like other Summerific hibiscus it emerges later than most perennials in spring but grows quickly once underway; plant in full sun in consistently moist, fertile soil for continuous bloom from midsummer to frost.

common_name: Glitter Bomb Hardy Hibiscus (Peppermint-Patterned Pink Red-Eyed Perennial Hibiscus, Summerific Series)

planting.note: Plant container plants or divisions in spring in consistently moist, fertile soil in full sun.

directions: This Walters Gardens Summerific introduction produces pink flowers patterned with a candy-striped, peppermint-like pattern and a prominent red eye, held above dark olive-green foliage. Its broad, mounded gumdrop habit spreads wider than it is tall, making it useful for filling space along the back of a border. Plant in full sun in consistently moist, fertile soil; like other Summerific hibiscus it is a fast-growing North American native that emerges late in spring but blooms continuously from midsummer to frost.

common_name: Head Over Heels Desire Hibiscus (True-Red Burgundy-Foliage Compact Hardy Hibiscus)

planting.note: Plant container plants in spring in moist, fertile soil in full sun; Head Over Heels Desire bears true-red, ruffled flowers against deep burgundy foliage on a dense, compact plant.

directions: Bred at Rutgers and released by Star Roses and Plants, Head Over Heels Desire opens large, ruffled, saucer-shaped true-red flowers from midsummer to early fall, set against glossy, dark green leaves tinted burgundy. The dense, bushy, compact habit and rich foliage color hold up well through the season. Grow in full sun in moist, fertile soil; like other Head Over Heels hibiscus it tolerates wet sites and is one of the last perennials to break dormancy in spring, so mark its location to avoid disturbing the crown.

common_name: Head Over Heels Dream Hibiscus (White Red-Centered Burgundy-Foliage Compact Hardy Hibiscus)

planting.note: Plant container plants in spring in moist, fertile soil in full sun; Head Over Heels Dream bears large white flowers with deep red centers against burgundy foliage on a dense, compact plant.

directions: The white-flowered member of the Rutgers-bred Head Over Heels series, Dream carries large, saucer-shaped white flowers with a bold red center held above dense, compact, dark green foliage tinted burgundy. It flowers from midsummer through early fall and, like its series-mates, makes a valuable late-season pollinator resource. Grow in full sun in moist, fertile soil; it tolerates wet sites and salt better than many hardy hibiscus and is slow to break dormancy in spring.

common_name: Torchy Hardy Hibiscus (Deep Red Glossy Perennial Hibiscus)

planting.note: Plant container plants or divisions in spring in consistently moist, fertile soil in full sun.

directions: This Fleming hybrid carries thick-textured, glossy, deep red to burgundy flowers against clean, three-lobed green foliage on an upright clump. Like other Fleming hardy hibiscus it is extremely cold hardy, tolerates heat, humidity, and periodic flooding once established, and draws bees, butterflies, and hummingbirds through its long midsummer-to-fall bloom season. Grow in full to mostly sun with regular moisture; it dies back completely each winter and re-emerges late in spring.

common_name: Dreamcatcher Hardy Hibiscus (Quilted Pale Pink Purple-Cast Foliage Perennial Hibiscus)

planting.note: Plant container plants or divisions in spring in consistently moist, fertile soil in full sun.

directions: Selected by Fleming breeders from a cross of Fleming H. moscheutos and H. coccineus lines, Dreamcatcher bears huge, thick-textured, quilted pale pink flowers on a compact, uniform clump of maple-shaped green leaves with a purple cast. It is extremely cold hardy and floriferous from midsummer until frost. Grow in full sun with consistently moist soil; expect it to die back completely each winter and emerge later than most perennial neighbors in spring.

common_name: Pink Comet Dwarf Hardy Hibiscus (White-and-Pink Red-Streaked Compact Perennial Hibiscus)

planting.note: Plant container plants or divisions in spring in consistently moist, fertile soil in full sun.

directions: A true dwarf among the Fleming hardy hibiscus introductions, Pink Comet produces flowers marked on both sides of the petals with tropical-looking streaks of red and pink over a white-and-pink ground, above shiny, maple-shaped green leaves. Bred from a multi-generation cross involving Fleming H. moscheutos and H. rosa-sinensis lines, it is nonetheless cold hardy once established and tolerates drought, wind, and flooding. Grow in full sun with regular moisture; it dies back to the ground each winter and re-emerges late in spring.

common_name: Strawberry Swirl Hardy Hibiscus (Pinwheel Pink-and-White Compact Perennial Hibiscus)

planting.note: Plant container plants or divisions in spring in consistently moist, fertile soil in full sun.

directions: Bred from Fleming H. moscheutos and H. coccineus seedlings, this compact cultivar produces large, bold pink-and-white flowers with a pinwheel-like swirled pattern above refined, maple-shaped green foliage. It is extremely cold hardy and blooms with vigorous, uniform floriferousness from midsummer until frost. Grow in full sun with consistently moist soil; it dies back completely each winter and is slow to emerge in spring.

common_name: Party Favor Hardy Hibiscus (Cotton-Candy Pink Red-Eyed Long-Blooming Perennial Hibiscus, Summerific Series)

planting.note: Plant container plants or divisions in spring in consistently moist, fertile soil in full sun.

directions: This Walters Gardens Summerific introduction opens rose-pink buds into glossy, cotton-candy-pink, heavily ruffled flowers with a red eye, produced at nodes all along the flowering stems rather than only at the top, for an especially long midsummer-to-frost bloom season. Highly dissected green leaves on red stems form a substantial clump. Grow in full sun in consistently moist, fertile soil; it emerges later than most perennials in spring but grows quickly once underway.
